prompts.title: Storytelling Thread / Carousel
prompts.description: LinkedIn or Twitter thread using Hero's Journey or StoryBrand — hook, struggle, insight, payoff.
prompts.template:
You are an expert narrative copywriter.

Write a {{postCount}}-part {{platform}} thread about {{topic}}.

Audience: {{audience}}
Story framework: {{storyFramework}}
Personal angle: {{personalAngle}}
Takeaway: {{takeaway}}
Tone: {{tone}}

Structure (label each post):
1. HOOK (contrarian or vulnerable opener — stop the scroll)
2. SETUP (ordinary world — relatable situation)
3. INCITING INCIDENT (what went wrong / changed)
4. STRUGGLE (2-3 posts — escalating difficulty, be specific)
5. INSIGHT (the turn — what you learned, the "aha")
6. TRANSFORMATION (proof it worked — numbers or moment)
7. LESSON (universal takeaway for {{audience}})
8. CTA (soft — {{callToAction}})

Each post: max {{maxChars}} characters. Line breaks for readability.
End with a one-line "Story map" naming each beat.

variables.name: takeaway
variables.label: Reader takeaway
variables.placeholder: you don't need a perfect plan — you need one scary first step

prompts.title: Curiosity Headline Pack
prompts.description: Headlines using curiosity gap, specificity, and open loops — for blogs, emails, and ads.
prompts.template:
You are an expert headline psychologist (curiosity gap, information gap theory).

Write {{count}} headlines for content about {{topic}}.

Audience: {{audience}}
Content type: {{contentType}}
Headline style mix: {{styleMix}}

For each headline provide:
- The headline (max {{maxChars}} chars)
- Curiosity type (gap / contrarian / number / question / how-to with twist)
- Open loop (what question it creates in the reader's mind)
- Subheadline option (one line that partially closes the loop)

Rules:
- Specific beats vague ('3 mistakes' beats 'common mistakes')
- No clickbait that the content can't deliver
- At least {{contrarianCount}} contrarian headlines

Rank top 3 by predicted CTR for {{audience}} with one-line rationale each.

exampleValues.topic: remote team productivity without more meetings

prompts.tips: Recommended when CTR matters more than SEO. Test top 3 in email subject lines first — fastest feedback loop. Curiosity gap fails if the article doesn't pay off the promise.

prompts.template:
You are an expert creative director writing prompts for AI image and video tools (Midjourney, DALL-E 3, Stable Diffusion, Runway, etc.).

Design an admin dashboard for {{appName}}.

Purpose: {{purpose}}
Primary users: {{users}}

Tech stack: {{techStack}}

Layout:
- Sidebar navigation with: {{navItems}}
- Top bar: search, notifications, user profile
- Main content area with:
  1. KPI cards row ({{kpiCount}} metrics)
  2. {{chartType}} chart (main visualization)
  3. Data table with sorting and filtering
  4. {{extraWidget}} widget

Design: {{designStyle}}. Color scheme: {{colors}}. Responsive: collapsible sidebar on mobile. Include loading states and empty states.

Output: A single copy-paste ready prompt optimized for AI generation.
Include technical details (lighting, lens, composition, aspect ratio hint).
End with: --ar 16:9 or --ar 1:1 if square format fits the use case.

colors.name: Blue
colors.firstImpression: Visitors feel safe and that the brand is reliable within the first 90 seconds.
colors.uxImpact: Strong for headers and navigation; CTA often works better in contrasting orange or green.
colors.caution: Overuse can feel cold or corporate if not balanced with warm neutrals.

colors.name: Red
colors.firstImpression: Immediate attention and emotional intensity — use sparingly for maximum effect.
colors.uxImpact: Highest click attention for CTAs; avoid large red backgrounds (raises stress).
colors.caution: Large red areas increase anxiety — reserve for buttons and accents.

colors.name: Green
colors.firstImpression: Signals freshness, approval, and positive action.
colors.uxImpact: Excellent for success states and primary CTAs in health/finance contexts.
colors.caution: Bright lime green can feel cheap — match saturation to price point.

colors.name: Orange
colors.firstImpression: Welcoming and action-oriented without red's aggression.
colors.uxImpact: Often the highest-converting CTA color against blue or white layouts.
colors.caution: Too much orange can feel discount-heavy — pair with neutrals for premium offers.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.firstImpression: Instant visibility — brain processes yellow first among colors.
colors.uxImpact: Great for badges and alerts; poor for body text (low readability).
colors.caution: Never use yellow for long text — accessibility and readability fail.

colors.name: Purple
colors.firstImpression: Premium or unconventional — stands out from blue-heavy competitors.
colors.uxImpact: Works as accent; deep purple feels luxury, bright purple feels playful.
colors.caution: Can reduce readability on dark purple backgrounds — check WCAG contrast.

colors.name: Black
colors.firstImpression: Premium and serious — fashion and high-ticket positioning.
colors.uxImpact: Use with generous whitespace; gold or white accents signal luxury.
colors.caution: Pure black (#000) on screens can feel harsh — use soft black (#0A0A0A).

colors.name: White & Cream
colors.firstImpression: Breathing room and modernity — lets product and copy lead.
colors.uxImpact: Essential for readability; pair with one strong accent for CTA.
colors.caution: All-white with no accent = invisible CTA — always define a conversion color.

colors.name: Pink
colors.firstImpression: Approachable and contemporary — expanded beyond traditional gender cues.
colors.uxImpact: Soft pink backgrounds + dark text = friendly; hot pink = bold Gen-Z energy.
colors.caution: Hot pink needs careful contrast checking for accessibility.

colors.name: Brown & Earth tones
colors.firstImpression: Authentic and grounded — artisan and natural products.
colors.uxImpact: Warm backgrounds increase time-on-page for storytelling brands.
colors.caution: Can feel dull without a fresh accent (green or cream).

colors.name: 藍色
colors.firstImpression: 訪客在 90 秒內感到安全，認為品牌可靠。
colors.uxImpact: 適合頁首與導覽；CTA 常用對比色（橙或綠）效果更好。
colors.caution: 過度使用易顯冷調或官僚感，需搭配暖色中性色平衡。

colors.name: 紅色
colors.firstImpression: 立即吸引注意與情緒強度 — 宜少量使用。
colors.uxImpact: CTA 點擊率最高之一；避免大面積紅底（增加壓力）。
colors.caution: 大面積紅色增加焦慮 — 保留給按鈕與強調。

colors.name: 綠色
colors.psychology: 成長、健康、平衡、金錢、自然
colors.firstImpression: 傳達新鮮、認可與正向行動。
colors.uxImpact: 成功狀態與健康／金融情境下的主 CTA 表現佳。
colors.caution: 亮萊姆綠可能顯廉價 — 飽和度需配合價位定位。

colors.name: 橙色
colors.firstImpression: 親切且導向行動，但比紅色溫和。
colors.uxImpact: 在藍色或白色版面上，常為轉換率最高的 CTA 色。
colors.caution: 橙色過多易顯折扣感 — 高單價需搭配中性色。

colors.name: 黃色
colors.firstImpression: 能見度最高 — 大腦最先處理黃色。
colors.uxImpact: 適合徽章與提醒；不適合長篇內文（可讀性差）。
colors.caution: 勿用黃色作長文字 — 無障礙與可讀性皆不佳。

colors.name: 紫色
colors.firstImpression: 高級或非主流 — 在藍色競爭中脫穎。
colors.uxImpact: 適合強調色；深紫顯奢華，亮紫顯活潑。
colors.caution: 深紫底上可讀性可能不足 — 需檢查 WCAG 對比。

colors.name: 黑色
colors.firstImpression: 高級且嚴肅 — 時尚與高單價定位。
colors.uxImpact: 搭配大量留白；金或白強調色強化奢華感。
colors.caution: 螢幕純黑 #000 可能過硬 — 建議用柔黑 #0A0A0A。

colors.name: 白色與奶油色
colors.firstImpression: 呼吸感與現代感 — 讓產品與文案成為主角。
colors.uxImpact: 可讀性必備；需搭配一個明確的 CTA 轉換色。
colors.caution: 全白無強調色 = CTA 消失 — 務必定義轉換色。

colors.name: 粉色
colors.firstImpression: 好接近且當代 — 已超越傳統性別刻板。
colors.uxImpact: 柔粉底 + 深字 = 友善；亮粉 = 大膽 Z 世代能量。
colors.caution: 亮粉需仔細檢查對比以符合無障礙。

colors.name: 棕色與大地色
colors.firstImpression: 真實、穩重 — 手工與天然產品。
colors.uxImpact: 暖色背景可延長故事型品牌的停留時間。
colors.caution: 若無清新強調色（綠或奶油）可能顯得沉悶。
